prompt_text: Who is the best interior painting company in St. Louis MO?
answer_verbatim:
There’s no single objectively “best” interior painting company for everyone — the right choice depends on your needs (home vs. business), budget, timeline, and neighborhood. I can certainly find highly rated options for you, but first a few quick questions so I can give the most useful recommendations:

- Is this for a residence or commercial property?
- Zip code or neighborhood in St. Louis?
- Approximate size (one room, whole house) and your target timeline/budget?
- Any special requirements (historic home, lead-safe certification, eco‑friendly paints)?

If you want to proceed right away, I can research top-rated local companies and return a short list (3–5) with ratings, typical prices, and contact info.

While you decide, here’s a short checklist and tips to help you choose the best painter:

Checklist when evaluating interior painters
- Reviews & reputation: Check Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, and the BBB for recent reviews and patterns.
- License & insurance: Confirm they carry general liability and workers’ comp.
- Written estimate: Get at least 2–3 detailed written bids that list prep work, number of coats, paint brand/finish, and timeline.
- Portfolio & references: Ask for before/after photos and references for similar work.
- Prep & cleanup: Make sure prep (patching, sanding, priming) and cleanup are included.
- Warranty/guarantee: Ask what they guarantee and how they handle touch-ups.
- Lead-safe: If your home was built before 1978, ask for EPA lead-safe credentials.
- Payment terms: Avoid large upfront payments; typical deposits are 10–30%.

Typical cost guidance (St. Louis, general range)
- Per square foot: roughly $2–6 per sq. ft. (varies by prep needs and paint quality)
- Per room: small bedroom often $300–800; large living areas or whole‑house jobs scale up accordingly
- Trim/ceiling/repairs: often extra; expect higher costs if extensive drywall or woodwork repair is needed

If you want, tell me your zip code and whether it’s residential/commercial and I’ll pull together a short list of highly rated interior painters in St. Louis with reviews and estimated pricing.
